newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Whirlpool to move Asia HQ to Hong Kong - paper.
newsitem.headline: Whirlpool to move Asia HQ to Hong Kong - paper.

text.p: American consumer electronics group Whirlpool Corp is closing its Singapore research and development centre and relocating its regional headquarters in Hong Kong, a report in the Straits Times said on Thursday.
Whirlpool officials were not immediately available for comment.
The reported move by the U.S. firm comes only a year after it announced plans to invest S$10 million in the research centre.

The newspaper quoted Bob Hall, president of Whirlpool Asia, as saying in a statement that it "is not efficient to maintain our regional HQ away from our key manufacturing regions -- India and greater China".
Hall said the company would consolidate its regional headquarters and move the executive team to Hong Kong to be closer to the majority of the group's businesses in Asia.
The restructuring would be completed by end of the year and the firm would lay off 150 of its staff in Singapore, the newspaper said.
